name: gtn: get the tutorial's own data into Galaxy, and get the real file
description: Split out from gtn-tutorial-completed, which stages a fixture and therefore never tests acquisition -- getting the data is a genuine part of completing a tutorial, and it was the untested half. Isolated deliberately: this one depends on an external host, so its flakiness stays here rather than spreading into the scenario that grades analysis. The trap is real and the tutorial walks into it: the URL printed on the GTN page returns an HTML redirect stub, not the file, and Galaxy accepts the stub without complaint, after which every downstream step works on the wrong data. Graded on what landed, not on what the agent says it fetched. The number assertion tolerates thousands separators: the model writes 1 596 with a narrow no-break space, and a bare \b1596\b reads a correct answer as a miss. Five turns, one per stage of the approval lifecycle: draft, approve, parameter table, approve again. A Zenodo transfer that fails mid-download is an environment failure and is recorded as one.
inputs: i want to run the data manipulation olympics gtn tutorial, can you find it for me and tell me what it's about
cool, lets pull the data for it and run it on this instance

yes, those parameters look right, go ahead and run it
